Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Start time: 10:00 AM PT / 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (CEO), Arjun Patel (CTO), Lina Chen (VP Product), Marcus Lee (Head of Eng), Priya Kapoor (Head of Research), Evan Brooks (Head of Sales), Rina Gomez (Head of CS), Tom Baker (CFO) + all employees (via webcast)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Q2 performance review: revenue, usage growth, churn, pipeline health; runway and hiring pause context.
- Product updates: Dedicated GA timeline, Private deployment improvements (VPC/on-prem), Console observability upgrades, Optimize recommendations.
- Research: inference perf wins, quantization/throughput work, benchmark results vs public baselines.

Topics: Q2 results; Dedicated & Private roadmap; Console/Optimize features; SOC 2 & security; hiring/hiring pause; customer success highlights.

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: All right, good morning, everyone, thanks for joining. Um, I know we've got people on the webcast and in the office, so we'll try to keep to an hour. Quick agenda — Q2 recap, product and engineering updates, security, and then Q&A.

[00:45] Tom Baker: Quick finance update — Q2 beat our top-line target by a touch, GAAP rev up 8% quarter-over-quarter, usage growth is healthy, but net-new logo conversion is slightly behind plan. We did take a conservative hiring pause for non-customer-facing roles, to preserve runway while we invest in Dedicated capacity.

[01:30] Sofia: Thanks Tom. The overall thesis stands — we prioritize serving and reliability, and we're doubling down on Dedicated and Private for enterprise buyers. Important note — we are not pausing hiring for critical product and infra roles.

[02:10] Evan Brooks: On sales — pipeline is strong in mid-market and a few enterprise deals that are Strategic. A few renewals went well, and we saw an increase in Dedicated inquiries post-benchmarks we published. We still need better collateral around procurement and procurement timelines.

[03:00] Lina Chen: Product updates — we shipped Console improvements: per-route token cost breakdown and tracing hooks, plus a small UX refresh. We're planning a GA announcement for Redwood Dedicated in late August; internal launch for early enterprise pilots next week.

[03:45] Marcus Lee: Engineering notes — the serving runtime had a few perf wins this quarter. The KV caching changes reduced tail latency on long-context workloads, although transcription here is saying "KV cash" sometimes, so apologies for the auto-transcribe. We landed a new kernel selection heuristic that helps on A100 and H100 variants. Some regressions popped up with a quantized Llama fork in staging but we caught them.

[04:30] Priya Kapoor: Research — we ran a set of benchmark evals vs published baselines (OpenAI, Anthropic). We saw 12-18% token throughput improvements on 4-bit quant runs on our testbed and latency improvements when using continuous batching + prefix caching. I'll publish the benchmark spreadsheet — it's linked in the follow-up. Note: some model names are auto-transcribed weirdly in notes.

[05:20] Arjun Patel: A bit more technical on Dedicated — the rollout plan is two phases: private pilot customers (VPC/on-prem options) then general availability with reserved capacity and burst policies. We're finalizing autoscaling policy defaults and resource shielding to maintain latency SLOs even under noisy neighbor workloads. We'll share the technical runbook; it will include kernel selection matrices per hardware SKU and sequence-length profiles.

[06:10] Rina Gomez: Customer Success highlights — CS has started a guided onboarding for Dedicated pilots to ensure customers configure caching, batching, and quant profiles to hit cost targets. We've seen customers trade cost for latency; we're documenting the best-practices playbook.

[06:50] Sofia: Security — where are we on SOC 2?

[07:00] Marcus Lee: SOC 2 Type II docs are in final review with external auditors; we expect certification next month. We're also rolling out KMS integration for Private deployments and HSM options for on-prem. Audit logs retention is configurable and will be part of the Private offering.

[07:40] Sofia: That's critical for enterprise. Also want to call out reliability work — we've improved our fallback policies so when a high-capacity region is constrained we can route to a lower-cost variant with graceful degradation. This is a key differentiator.

[08:10] Question from audience (text chat): Are we expanding regions?

[08:20] Arjun: Yes — more regions coming in APAC via cloud partners, timeline Q4. Initially for Dedicated and Private we will prioritize NA and EU for regulatory reasons.

[09:00] Lina: On product roadmap — high-level priorities for Q3 are: 1) Dedicated GA & pilot expansion, 2) Console observability (traces + token-level alerting), 3) Optimize features — smarter batching suggestions and per-model quant recommendations, 4) Private deployment polish (KMS, audit logs UI).

[10:15] Priya: Quick note on evals — we're introducing regression alerts tied to prompt sets and small automated tests that run on canary model releases. This should catch quality regressions earlier.

[11:00] Evan: Sales ops will need the Dedicated pricing sheet and a checklist for procurement; there are often long legal timelines for customers demanding private control planes, SSO/SAML, and data residency. We need to standardize negotiation templates.

[11:45] Tom: Financial ask — some of these Dedicated investments require short-term capital; proposing a small reallocation from hiring to capacity. We'll share a more detailed plan offline.

[12:30] Sofia: People update — hiring slowdown for non-customer-facing teams, but we still have open roles in platform infra, SRE, and a couple of product managers. We're focusing on retention and critical hiring. Any org changes? Not major; small adjustments in GTM to better support Dedicated motions.

[13:15] Live question: Will we open-source any of the kernel work?

[13:30] Priya: We will open-source some reference kernels and benchmarks, but not the full proprietary runtime optimizations. It's a balance — we want community trust but protect production IP.

[14:20] Sofia: Ok let's do a quick customer highlight — Rina, can you share one win?

[14:30] Rina Gomez: Sure — a mid-market SaaS customer moved from a self-hosted setup to Redwood Dedicated pilot, reducing per-token cost by ~25% with similar latency after tuning batch and cache settings. They cited better observability and rollback features as a big win during onboarding.

[15:10] Sofia: Great. Alright, open Q&A for the next chunk. Please use chat for questions.

[15:30] (Q&A session, various short questions about travel policy, expenses, events — auto-transcript noisy)

[20:45] Staff question (audio): Is there clarity on comp cycles given hiring pause?

[21:00] Tom: Compensation cycles are unchanged; promotions and manager reviews proceed as planned. We are focusing budgets on customer-facing growth levers.

[22:10] Sofia: Quick reminder on values and culture — we want to be transparent, shipping fast, and obsessed with product-market fit. If you have concerns about the hiring pause, talk to your manager or HR.

[23:00] Lina: Product folks — please review the Q3 roadmap doc; we'll solicit prioritized requests, but the three pillars are Dedicated, Console, Optimize.

[24:20] Marcus: Ops folks — we'll run a tabletop incident drill next month to validate fallback routing and model variant failover. Please sign up on the internal schedule.

[25:10] Priya: Research — we need eng help to instrument a perf test harness for long-context workloads. I'll follow up with a short RFC.

[26:00] Evan: Sales — we'll run a training on procurement playbooks and proposal templates; CS and legal are included.

[27:15] Sofia: Ok, final notes — we'll circulate the Q2 deck and a one-page summary. Expect the Dedicated runbook and pilot signup link in the follow-up. Thanks everyone.

[27:45] Sofia: Quick shout out to the infra team for the kernel work, and to CS for the recent pilot onboarding.

[28:10] (applause)

[28:30] Sofia: That's it. We'll close out — remember to review the follow-up doc and action items.
